full_judgment: 3. Facts necessary for disposal of the appeal may be stated thus: the appellant filed an application under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in respect of 4.09 acres of land alleging that taking advantage of his absence from home the respondents have been trying to dispose him which raised immediate apprehension of breach of peace. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate after receiving the report from the Officer-in-Charge of Satkania drew up proceedings under sub-section (I) of section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The disputed land was attached and the Circle Officer (Revenue) Satkania was appointed as the receiver. An application was filed by the respondents under sub-section (5) of section 145 for cancellation of aforesaid preliminary order, and it was rejected on November 7, 1973. Another application by the respondents for fresh local enquiry by a Magistrate or a high ranking Police Officer was also rejected by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate on November 20, 1973. Thereafter the respondents moved the Sessions, Judge Chittagong for making a reference to the High Court under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. But getting no relief from the Sessions Judge, they moved the High Court. As per direction of the High Court local enquiry was held by the Magistrate to whom the case was transferred. He prepared a memorandum and fixed October 21, 1975 for appearance of both parties. The appellant filed an application before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate under Section 523(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for withdrawing the case from the file of the aforesaid Magistrate alleging that he did not examine his witnesses produced at the time of local enquiry and had already formed opinion against him regarding possession of the disputed land. On this application the Sub-Divisional Magistrate passed an order on October 1, 1975 calling for the record and this order was communicated to the Magistrate on October 2, 1975. On the same date the Magistrate recorded an order to the effect that the record he sent to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate after October 21, 1975. The appellant filed an application before the Magistrate for staying further proceedings till the disposal of his transfer application, but the Magistrate refused to stay further proceedings on the ground that no stay order had been passed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. After recording this order the Magistrate dropped the proceedings under section 145(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The appellant moved the Sessions Judge who made the reference to the High Court with recommendation to set aside the aforesaid order of the Magistrate. From the judgment of the learned Single Judge of the High Court it appears that the learned Judge considered only one aspect of the case, i. e. whether there was materials before the Magistrate for dropping the proceedings under sub-section (5) of section 145. The learned Judge observed that in the instant case, the learned Magistrate had before him the petition filed by the second party who claimed that they had right, title and possession in the disputed land and that there was no apprehension of breach of peace; and that the learned Magistrate heard both the parties for two days and went to the locality, examined witnesses in presence of both the parties and was satisfied that there was no apprehension of breach of peace over the possession of the disputed land.
